steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Beat 1/2 cup butter, 1/2 cup peanut butter, white sugar, brown sugar, and vanilla in a large bowl until light and creamy. Add egg and beat until fully incorporated.
Whisk flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt together in a separate bowl. Add flour mixture to the peanut butter mixture and stir until just combined. Stir in oats until evenly incorporated.
Drop dough by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets. Flatten each mound with a fork to form 1/4-inch-thick cookies.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are lightly browned and centers are set, about 10 minutes. Let cool on the baking sheets briefly before transferring to wire racks to cool completely.

To make the filling: Cream 3 tablespoons butter with powdered sugar, 1/2 cup smooth peanut butter, and heavy whipping cream. Spread filling onto half of the cooled cookies, then top with the remaining cookies to form sandwiches.

review.reviewBody: This doesn't make a lot (approx. 15 cookies when put together, 22 using my smallest scooper), so when you double this, don't double the filling. It's more than enough ...trust me if you don't want to go into a sugar shock!!! lol A thin layer is plenty sweet. Thought this was useful to know, so ingredients aren't wasted. Also, when applying the filling especially when you get anxious like me, it's easier to do it while the cookie is on a flat surface instead of trying to hold it in your hand or raised. The cookie will break in half. 10 min. was perfect baking time. It helps to refrigerate for a little while to ensure cookies aren't flat, but definitely flatten w/fork. While it does flatten, to get that perfect cookie as pictured, it requires you to flatten a little. Using ingredients that are room temperature helps w/the overall consistency of the final product. These were a hit, and people are always amazed these were baked not bought!

I lived this recipe. I was looking for a great oatmeal peanut butter recipe I could add 3oz of m&m's too. So I made this with a little less of each sugar and I added back two tablespoons of stevia because i love the taste. I then split the dough in half in the bowl and scooped out the bottoms. I then addes the chocolate and mixed into the dough for the tops. This added a crunchy chocolate top to our sandwiches. Recipe asks for a teaspoon scoop but thata obviously too small. I used a 50 ot tablespoon scoop. It worked great and smashed them crisscross on top. The filling is great and I added some peanut butter powder and some water back for the filling for a more peanut butter rich cream filling. I definitely recommend this simple recipe. Be careful not to burn. You want them a little crispy so they hold together but just more than 9 mins was perfect. You need to let the cookies cool fully before trying to spread the filling. And make sure your filling is a peanut butter texture and not too dry. It will make for hard spreading. Enjoy!

So the first time I made these I followed the recipe to a tee. I found this searching for sourdough cookies ?? Anyway, I really wanted to incorporate sourdough starter to help use up my discard. So I messed around a couple of times. I increased the flour to 2/3 cup and added a 1/2 sourdough starter. The Starter should go in at the very end and only mix until blended. Let the dough sit for an hr. Cook for 12 minutes instead of 10. I personally prefer to do these as drop cookies. I stopped bothering with the filling it was way to sweet for me and my kids don't need the extra sugar.

I found this to be the perfect peanut butter cookie! I doubled the cookie recipe but not the icing -- there is plenty of icing. I didn't have quick cooking oats, so I blended a cup and 1/2 of rolled oats into a rough flour. I also substituted 3/4 of the sugar with Splenda and added a dash of molasses (to make 1/2c Splenda brown sugar). I used 1/2c regular brown sugar. For me, this balance of 3/4 splenda and 1/4 brown sugar worked out perfectly. I used very small amounts and pressed them VERY flat and shaped them perfectly round. If you don't press them very flat, your cookie sandwich is going to be too thick. My oven took 12 minutes, and the cookies are amazing!!

The recipe itself is very good; however, there are a few adjustments that I needed to make. The recipe states to put 1 teaspoon of batter on the baking sheet, but that can't be true, nor is it accurate. I used a #60 scooper (2 tsp equivalent) which is about the size of a melon-baller. I flattened them with a fork dipped in flour 'til they were 1/4 inch thick (as recipe states). They look small at first but get bigger/wider as they bake. They come out to the perfect size (not too big or too small). I baked them for only 6 minutes (til edges are light brown) and let them sit on the baking sheet afterwards for ~5min.

I followed the recipe exactly the first time I made them. I scooped my cookies with a cookie scoop and then halved the balls which gave a more manageable sized cookie. My husband and father-in-law preferred them refrigerated and loved them.
The second time I made the recipe I was in a hurry and was serving my gluten-free daughter. I exchanged gluten-free flour for regular flour and pressed the dough into a 9x13 pan and baked for 18minutes. I then spread the "filling" over the top as a frosting.. (I did not advertise that they were gluten-free to the rest of the eaters... and they were greatly enjoyed by all.)

These cookies were such a hit with the whole family. 
I did make a few changes. I doubled the cookie recipe because there just isn't enough batter. I did not have eggs so I substituted 3 tablespoons mayo for each egg. I used dark brown sugar instead of light. I kept the correct measurements for the filling but I used one tablespoon soy milk in place of the heavy whipping cream. Do pat the cookies down before baking and 9 minutes was long enough. Allow the cookies to fully cool before assembling with the filling. Soooooooooo good. :-)
The only reason I made so many changes is because I didn't have all the ingredients on hand.

Yum! Definitely a keeper. Very rich. I made a double batch of the cookies and a single batch of the filling as suggested by others. I was a little short on the filling, but the cookies are very worthy of eating plain. I dropped rounded teaspoons full on to parchment lined sheets. My regular cookie sheet took 8 min and the air sheet took 10 min. I didn't need to press the rounded teaspoons down before baking, they flattened perfectly when they cooled for 8-10 minutes. I also used milk for the filling instead of cream. Easy to make and are disappearing quickly as I type.

Every time I made these, they go FAST!! I get 30 cookies from the original recipe. I’ve made them with and without the cream filling. I’d suggest making smaller cookies as the larger ones are difficult to eat, not that it stops anyone. The cream filling is scrumptious!! One little change I make is I use crunchy peanut butter. Next batch I’m trying butterscotch chips, but only half of the cookies. I don’t want to ruin the whole batch!!

My Husband and Son LOVED them! I didn't have heavy whipping cream, so I made some. Just Melt 1/3 C. butter in a saucepan then add the 2/3 C. milk and stir over medium low heat until combined. (You can also use the microwave and melt butter, heat up milk for 20 seconds and combine)

Great Recipe, made it using ingredients exactly as stated in the recipe, and they came out great. I needed a cookie recipe to bake for a meeting at work where we all have to bring cookies for everyone, so I doubled the cookie recipe, and did 1 and a half of the filling recipe, and it ended up being a perfect amount. (Made about 22 large cookie sandwiches.)
Note: you do really have to like peanut butter, since it's in the cookie, AND the filling. 

Tips/Modifications: 
- I did refrigerate my dough for a few minutes before forming the cookies, and in between batches. 
- I ended up using teaspoon sizes scoops to form each cookie, because I thought the size stated in the recipe were too small... My cookies actually came out quite big, like regular sized cookies, but mini cookies might have been better in this case because 1) they're cookie sandwiches, and 2) they are rich. 
- I added vanilla PASTE to my filling in my second batch, and it made the filling taste so much better! I do recommend it; though, I'm not sure how adding vanilla extract would taste. 
- Also, I only put the cookies in the oven for 8 minutes, and let sit on the tray for about 30 seconds longer, before moving them to a cooling rack. The tip to move the oven rack one slot down to ensure a crisp bottom was great; it made frosting the cookies easier.
Hey, Girl Scout cookies are good but these are actually better, or so my family says. Admittedly I use a little less filling, but these are great.
Refrigerate batter before baking

I followed the directions exactly. I was really looking forward to the Girl Scout cookie taste that I love. The cookie part was ok, but the spread was nothing like GS cookies. It was way too sweet. I suppose I could alter the recipe and use less sugar. I don’t think I will make these again. I will eat the cookies without the spread and continue to buy GS cookies! Thanks for sharing the recipe.

I accidentally melted my butter for the filling when I tried to soften it, so I put in extra confectioner's sugar to make it fluffier. I also beat the peanut butter/butter/vanilla/sugar mixture more than the recipe called for, but it made the cookies lighter and bigger. I didn't have heavy whipping cream either, so I used Silk Half-and-half substitute.
Everyone loved this cookies, my family, co-workers, my doctor and friends. This is a great recipe. They are not to sweet and taste amazing. I did not change anything.
These taste like Girl Scout peanut butter sandwich cookies - so yummy!
I saw this picture of the cookies online, and I said OMG I have to make those. Super easy to make and everyone loved them. Definitely a keeper!

Wonderful! Really does have the flavor of the Girl Scout cookies. Our whole family loved it, including the picky-about-peanut-butter mom. I pretty much followed the recipe except I added an extra 1/2 c of oats because the batter seemed to "fluffy" and I doubled the batter but not the frosting since everyone said it made too much. In retrospect, I shouldn't have done either. I ended up with frosting-less cookies (which still tasted great!) and they're a bit dry. Still excellent, though!
These are the BEST cookies!!! I don’t make them into sandwich cookies and add chocolate chips or other things like white chocolate chips, nuts, coconut, toffee ect… Always come out perfect!!!
